Find co-expressologs across all species pairs

Source: R/comparison.R
find_coexpressologs.Rd

Runs the full comparison pipeline for each species pair and combines the results into a single edge data frame ready for find_cliques.

find_coexpressologs(networks, ...)

# Default S3 method
find_coexpressologs(
  networks,
  orthologs,
  species_pairs = NULL,
  method = c("analytical", "permutation"),
  alternative = c("greater", "less"),
  alpha = 0.05,
  n_cores = 1L,
  use_torch = FALSE,
  min_exceedances = 50L,
  max_permutations = 10000L,
  pi0_method = c("randomized", "storey", "none"),
  pval_combine = c("max", "min"),
  filter_zero = FALSE,
  seed = NULL,
  out_file = NULL,
  rho0 = NULL,
  ...
)

run_pairwise_comparisons(...)

Arguments

networks

Named list of compute_network outputs, keyed by species abbreviation.

...

Additional arguments passed to the default method.

orthologs

Data frame with columns Species1, Species2, hog (from parse_orthologs or extract_orthologs).

species_pairs

Optional list of length-2 character vectors specifying which pairs to compare. Defaults to all combn(names(networks), 2).

method

Testing method: "analytical" (default, fast) or "permutation" (rigorous).

alternative

"greater" (conservation, default) or "less" (divergence).

alpha

Significance threshold (default 0.05).

n_cores

Number of threads (default 1).

use_torch

Logical. Use GPU-accelerated fold-enrichment precomputation for permutation method (default FALSE).

min_exceedances

Besag-Clifford stopping parameter for permutation method (default 50).

max_permutations

Maximum permutations for permutation method (default 10000).

pi0_method

Analytical method only: how pi0 is estimated for the pair-level Storey q-values, passed to summarize_comparison: "randomized" (default), "storey" or "none" (Benjamini-Hochberg). The default draws; pass seed to pin those draws.

pval_combine

Analytical method only: how the two directional q-values are combined, passed to comparison_to_edges: "max" (default; both directions significant – the reciprocal criterion of Netotea et al. (2014), the Max.p.val filter of the original ComPlEx) or "min" (permissive; either direction, denser edge supply for find_cliques).

filter_zero

Analytical method only: passed to summarize_comparison. FALSE (default) keeps every tested ortholog pair, including those whose neighbourhood overlap is zero in either direction, so a pair that could not have been called still reaches the edge table carrying its power. Those are exactly the low-degree failures the power column exists to mark; dropping them hands the clique classifiers an untested-looking gap instead of an underpowered one. TRUE removes them before the q-values are computed, which is what canonical ComPlEx does – it shrinks the multiple-testing set, so every q-value moves.

seed

Integer seed for the call's random draws, or NULL (default) to draw from the global RNG. Seeding here makes the call reproducible, and with it every downstream count thresholded on q.value. The seed is applied once, for the whole species-pair loop, rather than being handed to each summarize_comparison call: one seeded stream flows through the pairs in order, so each pair draws its own uniforms instead of every pair reusing the same ones.

What a seed buys differs by method. Under "analytical" it pins the randomized-p draws behind pi0, and the result is reproducible at any n_cores. Under "permutation" it pins the per-thread seeds that the C++ engines draw from R's RNG, which reproduces the run at n_cores = 1 only: above that the OpenMP guided schedule decides which thread takes which HOG, so the pairing of thread streams to HOGs still moves between runs.

A seeded call draws from a private stream and restores the caller's on exit; with seed = NULL the draws come from the ambient stream and leave it advanced. Same contract as detect_modules and summarize_comparison.

out_file

Optional path to a CSV file. When supplied, each species pair's edge table is appended to out_file via fwrite as soon as it is computed, instead of being accumulated in memory and combined with rbind() at the end. This keeps peak memory bounded by one pair's edge table rather than the whole run, which matters for many species / dense networks. Any existing file at out_file is overwritten (not appended to) at the start of the call. When out_file is used, this function always creates out_file – including a header-only file when no species pair produces any edges – and returns out_file (invisibly) instead of a data frame; read the result back with e.g. data.table::fread(out_file). Not supported on the rcomplex S3 method (see find_coexpressologs.rcomplex), which stores the in-memory edge table on $edges. Default NULL keeps the original in-memory behaviour.

rho0

Analytical method only: reference fold enrichment for the power column, passed to comparison_to_edges (default NULL, the median effect size of the called pairs). The permutation path always reports power = NA: its HOG-level q-value has no per-pair call threshold to measure power against.

Value

Data frame with columns gene1, gene2, species1, species2, hog, q.value, effect_size, jaccard, power, type (power is NA under method = "permutation"). Ready for find_cliques or classify_cliques. When out_file is supplied, the edge table is streamed to that file instead (always created, even when empty), and out_file is returned (invisibly).

Methods

analytical

Fast path: pair-level Storey q-values via summarize_comparison. Appropriate when most HOGs are single-copy.

permutation

Rigorous path: gene-identity permutation via permutation_hog_test with Besag-Clifford adaptive stopping and Liang discrete q-values. Required for multi-copy HOGs where pair-level tests are correlated.

Gene universe

Each network is built on all genes supplied to compute_network and the hypergeometric population is the whole network (Netotea et al. 2014). Canonical ComPlEx implementations restrict expression to ortholog genes before building the networks; that changes neighbourhoods and calls, so rcomplex matches them only when the expression matrices are restricted the same way beforehand (see compare_neighborhoods).

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Fast analytical path; seed pins the randomized pi0 draws
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs, seed = 1)

# Canonical ComPlEx calls: reciprocal criterion (default) + plain BH
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs, pi0_method = "none")

# Permissive either-direction calls (denser clique input)
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs, pval_combine = "min")

# Rigorous permutation path with GPU
edges <- find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs,
  method = "permutation", use_torch = TRUE, n_cores = 4L
)

# Stream edges to disk instead of holding every pair in memory
find_coexpressologs(networks, orthologs, out_file = "edges.csv")
edges <- data.table::fread("edges.csv")
} # }
